headline: Gulf lenders and producers gear up for postwar boom as oil output nears pre-war levels
bottomLine: Gulf finance is positioning for a postwar upswing: a First Abu Dhabi bank has raised 15 billion dirhams (about $4.1 billion), and OPEC says oil production is nearing pre-war levels, with Brent at $92.14. The mood is less settled in markets, where Gulf sovereign wealth funds are reported to be among those hit by the AI sell-off, a test for the technology push that dominated last week's brief. Macro dispersion remains wide: Egypt's inflation of 14.1% contrasts with 0.7% in Morocco and -0.1% in Bahrain, and Qatar's current-account surplus of 14.8% of GDP contrasts with Jordan's 5.3% deficit (2024). Washington says the Iran war is 'effectively over' militarily, but no imminent deal is seen and it says it is ready to resume strikes if needed.
notableFlows: A First Abu Dhabi bank has raised 15 billion dirhams (about $4.1 billion) to fund what the market is calling the postwar boom, a sign that UAE lenders expect credit demand to rebuild as the regional conflict fades. The reported size makes it one of the larger local-currency fundraisings of the week.

Gulf sovereign wealth funds are reported to be among the investors hit by the AI sell-off, after a run of large technology commitments. Mark-to-market losses on AI-linked holdings could slow the pace of new overseas tech deals, though the funds' long horizons and scale cushion the impact.

Trump said he was unaware of a reported $500 million deal between World Liberty Financial and a UAE counterparty, drawing attention to the political exposure of Gulf-linked crypto and finance ties. Details of the transaction remain thin, and its terms have not been independently confirmed.

OPEC says oil production is nearing pre-Iran-war levels, indicating that Gulf export capacity is largely restored. With Brent at $92.14, producers are recovering volumes while importers such as Egypt and Jordan get some relief on their energy bills.

techJobs.context: AI-estimated: Gulf hiring in data-centre, cloud and AI roles continues to grow, though the AI-equity sell-off could slow new postings; note that the youth unemployment figures are also approximate AI estimates, as no WDI youth data was available this week.

risks.title: Iran settlement unresolved despite military de-escalation
risks.description: Since last week: Trump has said the Iran war is 'effectively over' militarily and further strikes are unlikely, and OPEC says oil output is nearing pre-war levels. But no imminent deal is seen before Trump meets mediator Qatar, Washington says it is ready to resume strikes if necessary, and fighting grips Yemen while Qatar and Turkey have signed a defence deal. Brent at $92.14 (up 2.2%) shows the market prices in calm, leaving it exposed if talks stall.

risks.title: AI sell-off tests Gulf sovereign tech strategy
risks.description: Gulf sovereign wealth funds are reported to be among those hit by the AI sell-off, following the large technology deals covered last week, including reported PIF talks over Unity. Further falls in AI-linked valuations would lower paper returns on overseas tech stakes and could make funds more selective on new commitments.

risks.title: External financing gaps at oil importers
risks.description: Jordan ran a current-account deficit of 5.3% of GDP in 2024 with growth of 2.8% in 2025, and Egypt combines 14.1% inflation with a 3.8% deficit. Brent at $92.14 is a manageable import bill, but both economies would feel any renewed energy price jump quickly.
